finalists.label: Lichen planopilaris
finalists.why: It has specific findings such as dermoscopic examination results and negative hair pull test that are unique to this condition.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation on dermoscopic examination, which are characteristic of Lichen planopilaris, decided the final comparison.

support_spans: inflammatory infiltrates between adipocytes with hyaline fat necrosis in the subcutis
Direct immunofluorescence: Positive with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels
Dermoscopic examination of the alopecic area revealed several short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation
2 long, curved-line, depressed, alopecic patches on the left side of the vertex and frontal scalp area extending to the left eyebrow
result of a hair pull test was negative
contradict_spans: inflammatory infiltrates between adipocytes with hyaline fat necrosis in the subcutis
